mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Friday 4:09 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-20 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: NVIDIA Corp
items.about: Nvidia designs the graphics processors and computing systems that power most AI data centers.
items.why: Nvidia closed about 14% lower after Reuters reported in the afternoon that the SEC is examining its accounting, citing two people briefed on the matter; the SEC declined to comment and no wrongdoing has been established. The drop extends a slide that began with the board's Nov 8 probe of Jensen Huang and his Nov 12 resignation, and it pulled chip stocks sharply lower.

items.name: Invesco QQQ Trust
items.about: QQQ tracks the Nasdaq-100, the 100 largest non-financial companies on the Nasdaq.
items.why: The Nasdaq-100 fund fell about 5.5% as chipmakers led a broad tech selloff, with Nvidia, AMD and Micron each down 12–14%. Posts focus on the Reuters report of an SEC review of Nvidia's accounting and on fears of forced selling and margin calls next week.

items.name: Capricor Therapeutics
items.about: Capricor develops cell therapies, led by deramiocel for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
items.why: Capricor edged up about 1% and traded higher after hours as holders positioned for the FDA's Nov 22 target date for deramiocel, which was pushed back from Aug 22 after the company filed a major amendment with HOPE-3 extension data. An FDA advisory panel voted 9–3 in July against its effectiveness for DMD heart disease; posts say a decision could land Monday.

items.name: IREN Limited
items.about: IREN runs data centers that rent out GPU cloud capacity for AI and mine bitcoin.
items.why: IREN fell about 18% as AI data-center and GPU-cloud stocks sold off alongside Nvidia. Posts point to worries that cheaper, smaller AI models could leave too much computing capacity, while others cite its Microsoft contract; no company-specific news was confirmed.

items.name: Micron Technology
items.about: Micron makes DRAM and NAND memory chips, including high-bandwidth memory used in AI servers.
items.why: Micron fell about 14% in the semiconductor rout that deepened after the Reuters report on Nvidia's accounting. No Micron-specific news was found; posts frame it as an unwind of the AI-memory trade after a big run.

items.name: Take-Two Interactive
items.about: Take-Two publishes video games including Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption and NBA 2K.
items.why: Take-Two rose about 0.8% on a day most tech fell, as Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale Nov 19 after Sensor Tower estimated about 15.9 million digital preorders worth about $1.5 billion. Posts say day-one sales hit $3.79 billion, but Take-Two has not published launch figures yet; BofA expects initial numbers by Nov 23.

items.name: Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X
items.about: SOXL aims to return three times the daily move of a semiconductor stock index.
items.why: The triple-leveraged chip fund lost about 32% as semiconductor stocks fell roughly 10% (SMH -10.5%), led by Nvidia, AMD and Micron. Posts say semis had their worst week in decades; the daily 3x reset magnifies losses in volatile stretches.

items.name: Strategy
items.about: Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) holds a large bitcoin treasury funded with stock and debt, alongside a software business.
items.why: Strategy fell about 9.6% as bitcoin and crypto stocks slid with the wider risk-off move. A November report said bitcoin had dipped below Strategy's average purchase cost of about $75,451 per coin; the stream is heavily bearish.

items.name: Applied Digital
items.about: Applied Digital builds and runs data centers for AI and high-performance computing customers.
items.why: Applied Digital fell about 18% as AI data-center builders sold off with Nvidia. Posts cite a Bloomberg report that ING's roughly $500 million auction of data-center loans drew weak bids, adding to worries about how the AI buildout is financed.

items.name: VanEck Semiconductor ETF
items.about: SMH holds about 25 of the largest US-listed chipmakers and chip-equipment companies.
items.why: The chip ETF fell about 10.5% as Nvidia, AMD and Micron each dropped 12–14% after the Reuters report on an SEC review of Nvidia's accounting. Posts say it was the fund's worst week since 2001.

items.name: ProShares UltraPro QQQ
items.about: TQQQ aims to return three times the daily move of the Nasdaq-100.
items.why: The 3x Nasdaq-100 fund fell about 16% as the index lost about 5.5% in the chip-led selloff. Posts debate whether it retests its 2026 low near $37.

items.name: BitMine Immersion Technologies
items.about: BitMine holds a large ether treasury and runs bitcoin-mining operations.
items.why: BitMine fell about 14% as crypto-linked stocks dropped with digital-asset prices in the broad risk-off move. No company-specific news was found; posts mostly react to the price drop.

items.name: iShares Russell 2000 ETF
items.about: IWM tracks the Russell 2000 index of small US companies.
items.why: Small caps fell about 2.7%, less than the Nasdaq, as selling spread beyond tech. Fed officials have floated a possible hike at the Dec 8–9 meeting, which weighs on rate-sensitive small companies; posts are split on whether a bounce is near.

items.name: Advanced Micro Devices
items.about: AMD designs CPUs and GPUs for PCs, servers and AI data centers.
items.why: AMD fell about 13% in the chip selloff, after losing about 8% on Nov 19. Posts tie it to the Nvidia accounting report and doubts about AI spending; no AMD-specific news was found.

items.name: SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF
items.about: DIA tracks the 30-stock Dow Jones Industrial Average.
items.why: The Dow fund fell about 1.8%, holding up better than tech as money rotated toward consumer staples and Treasuries. The stream is heavily bearish, with talk of margin calls and the VIX near 30.

items.name: Nebius Group
items.about: Nebius rents out GPU cloud capacity and AI infrastructure from data centers in Europe and the US.
items.why: Nebius fell about 16% as AI cloud and data-center names sold off with Nvidia. No company-specific news was found; posts note the Nasdaq's steep drop and debate a rebound.

items.name: MARA Holdings
items.about: MARA mines bitcoin and holds bitcoin on its balance sheet.
items.why: MARA fell about 19% as bitcoin miners dropped with crypto prices and the wider market. Posts criticize management over a recently announced deal they put at about $79 million, a figure that is not confirmed.

items.name: ProShares Ultra VIX Short-Term Futures ETF
items.about: UVXY gives leveraged exposure to short-term VIX futures, which rise when markets expect turbulence.
items.why: The volatility fund jumped about 22% as the VIX climbed toward 30 during the selloff. Because it holds rolling futures with leverage, it tends to lose value when volatility calms.

items.name: iShares Silver Trust
items.about: SLV holds physical silver and tracks the metal's price.
items.why: The silver fund fell about 6.7% as metals were sold along with stocks and crypto. Posts say traders dumped metals to cover margin calls, and some note falling commodity prices are easing inflation worries.

items.name: Sarepta Therapeutics
items.about: Sarepta develops genetic medicines for rare neuromuscular diseases such as Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
items.why: Sarepta fell about 5.9% with the market, extending its slide since an earnings miss and a reported DMD trial setback in early November. The company still guides for multiple-ascending-dose data in DM1 and FSHD in Q4 2026, which posts are watching.
